guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (asynchronous reset), prng_reseed_done_q is set to 1'b0, rnd_ctr_q is cleared to all zeros ('0), and num_rounds_q is cleared to all zeros ('0).
On every posedge clk_i when rst_ni is high, prng_reseed_done_q is updated with prng_reseed_done_d, rnd_ctr_q with rnd_ctr_d, and num_rounds_q with num_rounds_d.

assumptions.claim: num_rounds_d must be a valid AES round count (e.g., 10, 12, or 14) because the stored value will be used by downstream FSM logic to determine the number of encryption rounds.
assumptions.cond: when rst_ni is high and a clock edge occurs
assumptions.risk: An invalid round count could cause encryption with wrong number of rounds, leading to incorrect ciphertext/plaintext and possibly breaking AES security guarantees.

assumptions.claim: rnd_ctr_d must remain within the proper range (typically 0 to num_rounds−1) to avoid overflow or illegal state progression; the register does not check bounds.
assumptions.cond: when rst_ni is high and a clock edge occurs
assumptions.risk: If rnd_ctr_d exceeds num_rounds_d, the round counter may overrun, causing the FSM to loop indefinitely or access an undefined state, potentially stalling the cipher or exposing intermediate values.

assumptions.claim: prng_reseed_done_d must be asserted only after the PRNG reseed operation has truly completed and the entropy source is stable; the register latches the value without qualification.
assumptions.cond: when the design exits reset and begins operation
assumptions.risk: A glitch or premature assertion could set prng_reseed_done_q high, allowing the cipher to start before sufficient entropy is available, compromising the security of key derivation or masking.
